patch.description: Nonlinear Landau damping (collisionless relaxation of plasma waves) and long-time kinetic stability proven beyond the idealized setting: Sobolev (finite-regularity) data, whole space, bounded domains with absorbing or emitting walls, magnetized plasmas, weak collisions and full electromagnetic (Vlasov-Maxwell) fields, with explicit rates. These say when and how fast kinetic fluctuations damp, which is what fluid closures try to imitate.
patch.merge_note: A1: merged plasma-landau-longtime (same problem; identical years 2029/2027/2027 and bands Medium/High/High). Kept the frontier id and its sourcing (Mouhot-Villani Lean-formalized by Bedrossian Sep 2026; Ionescu-Nguyen unconfined 2D Sep 2026; family 362 at T3 as a prerequisite for long-time questions, not a decay result). Added plasma's bounded-domain/wall variants and its downstream role: the hard edge to plasma-kinetic-closures (which Landau-fluid terms are legitimate) now originates here. Public access (cap-research-math-public) is kept as a soft accelerator, since labs can pose the problem internally.

patch.description: Hardness-of-approximation ceilings for the combinatorial problems behind constellation tasking, ground-station and gateway siting, routing, beam frequency assignment and network partitioning become verified theorems rather than beliefs: beating Goemans-Williamson Max-Cut (beam two-colouring) or factor-2 vertex cover (minimal link/beam sets) is NP-hard under UGC; uniform sparsest cut (mesh partitioning) has no constant-factor algorithm; metric k-median siting is pinned at 1+2/e. Planning tools and vendor claims are judged against known limits.
patch.merge_note: A1: merged comms-hardness-ceilings-settled (same families 102/117/125/124/110/111, same years 2027 and bands High in all scenarios). Kept the frontier id. Took comms' finer premise audit: 102 Lean covers the UGC theorem and vertex cover below 2 (T3); 117's Lean main result is the SDP integrality gap, so the NP-hardness headline is T1 (statement gap); 125's Lean covers a companion recovery result, so the (1+2/e+eps) algorithm headline is T1 pending audit; 124, 110, 111 are T1 (conditional parts). High band rests on the T3 core (102) and the fact that most ceilings were already believed; P3 acts within months of an independent check.

patch.description: Proofs of the ultimate rates of the optical and quantum channels used for deep-space laser links, optical relays serving several receivers and satellite QKD: 273 (entropy photon-number inequality) makes the optical broadcast-channel capacity region and the thermal-noise optical wiretap secret-key capacity unconditional; 276 gives the exact classical capacity of every qubit generalized amplitude-damping channel; 272 (entangled states with zero distillable key; PPT-squared disproof) says link entanglement does not certify key; 266 (exactly three MUBs in dimension six) confirms prime-power dimensions for high-dimensional QKD.
patch.merge_note: A1: merged comms-optical-capacity-theory (273) and comms-quantum-channel-limits (276, 266, 272); the frontier node already covered exactly this union. Years agree (2028/2027/2027, S1 2027 for the 276 part). Bands kept at frontier's Low/Medium/Medium because the headline premise 273 is T1 and the framework requires 'conditional' plus a one-band drop; the 276 component alone (Lean OAI.GAD.main, T3, unchecked by outsiders) would rate Medium/High/High, and comms' Medium/High/High for 273 did not apply the drop. Comms sourcing retained: Lean-QIT (arXiv 2607.09632) formalizes HSW, so an S2 agent can formalize 273 during 2027. comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs now takes this node as a soft accelerator (finite-key security proofs do not require these capacity results to be settled).

patch.title: AI finds a crack in post-quantum or space-link crypto (watch item)
patch.description: Watch item, not a forecast: an AI-produced, independently verified cryptanalytic result that materially lowers the security of a standardized primitive used on satellite command and data links, above all ML-KEM/ML-DSA or the Module-LWE problems beneath them (for example 10+ bits off a parameter set, or a subexponential module-lattice algorithm), but also elliptic-curve schemes or AES modes, forcing parameter or algorithm changes and in-orbit re-keying on long-lived spacecraft.
patch.merge_note: A1: merged comms-lattice-weakness (S2 2028, S3 2027) and capability-crypto-watch (S2 2030, S3 2029); all three were the same watch item with Speculative/Low/Low bands and the same non-attack families (279, 138). Kept the frontier id and its middle years (>2031/2029/2028). Added comms' evidence: Olejnik-Naskrecki agent workflow broke eight non-standardized academic constructions (Aug 2026); Luo arXiv 2605.17412 claims a quantum Module-LWE attack over 2-power cyclotomics, unrefereed and unendorsed; a similar 2024 claim was withdrawn. comms-ai-cryptanalysis (agents audit crypto at research grade) is now a hard prerequisite. Dropped 272/266 from the family list: they refine QKD theory and are not attacks.

patch.title: Stiff chemistry with certified error (reduced mechanisms and solvers)
patch.description: Error theory, reduced kinetic mechanisms and verified structure-preserving stiff ODE/DAE integrators for large reaction networks (combustion, ablation, plasma chemistry, batteries), with provable error bounds on ignition delay, heat release and key species that hold for non-dissipative chemistry. First engineering use: detailed LOX/CH4 and LOX/H2 chemistry inside engine LES at a fraction of today's cost (chemistry integration dominates reacting-flow cost: 48,000 core-hours for 2 ms of one 54-species spray LES, UConn 2023).
patch.merge_note: A1: merged prop-stiff-chemistry (same achievement; identical prerequisites, years 2030/2028/2028, bands Medium/High/High and family 149 at T1, conditional and marginal). Kept the frontier id as the general node; prop's engine-LES framing and 3-10x reacting-LES cost estimate (general) are carried in the description. prop-flame-response and prop-start-transient keep their hard dependency, now on this node.

patch.description: Moment-SOS, tight convex relaxations, branch-and-bound and MIP methods that certify a trajectory, layout or design is globally optimal, or within a proven gap, at engineering scale, using sparsity, symmetry and convergence-rate theory. First applications: low-thrust, multi-body and rendezvous trajectories ('within 0.5% of the best possible' instead of 'best we found').
patch.merge_note: A1: merged astro-global-optimality-certificates (same methods and achievement; identical years 2030/2028/2027 and bands Medium/High/High). Kept the frontier id. Added astro's evidence: DA Taylor expansions plus moment-SOS with guaranteed convergence on low-thrust CR3BP station-keeping (Evans, Fossa, Armellin, Henrion, Zanetti, arXiv 2607.15801, Jul 2026); sparse Lasserre with GPU ADMM (STROM, arXiv 2406.05846). Scaling to many-revolution transfers remains open.

patch.description: Embedded SOCP/QP solvers for powered-descent guidance, rendezvous MPC and collision avoidance with machine-checked proofs that, in the flight processor's floating-point arithmetic, they terminate within a fixed iteration budget and return an epsilon-feasible, epsilon-optimal solution or a certified infeasibility flag for every admissible state, paired with cheap runtime certificates (duality gaps) checked each control cycle. One reusable certified component for landers, docking systems and collision-avoidance planners.
patch.merge_note: A1: merged astro-verified-onboard-solver (same achievement: a proven onboard convex solver). verif had rated it 2031/2029/2028 Low/Medium/Medium with a qualification gate because it bundled timing evidence on radiation-tolerant processors and HIL; astro rated it 2030/2028/2027 Medium/High/High as a formalization milestone. Reconciled by scoping this node to the proofs plus runtime certificates (all hard prerequisites, including infra-verified-numerics and verif-verified-gnc-numerics, land by S2 2028), and leaving flight timing/HIL qualification to verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight and verif-hls-autonomy-certification. Astro's caution kept: a Jun 2026 audit found compilation-based metrics overstate numerical-analysis formalization quality (arXiv 2606.14000).

patch.title: A lander flies proof-checked descent guidance and fault logic
patch.description: A lunar lander (or, as a first step, a vertical-landing test vehicle) flies terminal-descent GNC whose key properties are machine-checked, not only Monte Carlo-tested: convergence, feasibility and solver numerics of the powered-descent guidance, plus altitude plausibility, measurement-rejection gates, engine-cutoff and reboot logic. Its assumptions are red-teamed against terrain and sensor models.
patch.merge_note: A1: merged astro-landing-guidance-proven-flight (same milestone: first flight of proof-checked descent software; astro 2031/2029/2028 Low/Medium/High, verif 2030/2029/2028 Medium/High/High). Kept the verif id and its failure record (Schiaparelli, Beresheet, Hakuto-R M1, IM-1, Athena). The merged node now requires both guidance-solver proofs (verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates, astro-certified-gnc-toolchain, astro-scp-guarantees) and fault-logic checks, so bands take the stricter astro view. Full chain (S2): research-grade applied math public 2027 -> verified numerics and solver proofs 2028 -> GNC toolchain adopted 2028 -> software freeze 12-18 months before flight -> first flight 2029-30 on a CLPS-class lander or terrestrial testbed; launch cadence and software freeze bind, not cognition. No regulator is involved for commercial lunar landers, so no Medium cap.

patch.title: Assured autonomous docking, servicing and propellant transfer
patch.description: Rendezvous, proximity operations, docking, servicing or debris capture, and ship-to-ship propellant transfer flown with machine-checked passive safety (collision-free under failures), keep-out zones, abort reachability and capture logic, plus runtime assurance on the guidance, used as primary safety evidence.

Confidence is gated by flight demonstrations and launch cadence, not proof capacity.

patch.title: Crewed GNC autonomy certified with AI proofs
patch.description: NASA human-rating (NPR 8705.2C with NPR 7150.2 Class A software), FAA commercial human-spaceflight rules or ECSS accept AI-produced machine-checked proofs as part of the certification evidence for crew-critical GNC autonomy (landing guidance, docking, abort and fault management). The likeliest first case is a block upgrade for a crewed lunar lander.

patch.description: Certification authorities (FAA via DO-178C, DO-333 and DO-330; NASA software assurance under NPR 7150.2; ECSS; Space Force) grant project-level credit for formal proofs written by AI agents on the 'checker, not generator' route: an already-qualified checker (SPARK GNATprove, Frama-C WP, Astree) or a newly qualified small kernel (Lean or Comparator) verifies the proofs, so the agent needs no tool qualification and human obligations shrink to reviewing specifications and justifying assumptions.

patch.title: Upper-atmosphere density and drag with honest error bars
patch.description: Thermospheric density nowcasts and 1-3 day forecasts with calibrated uncertainty, cutting quiet-time error from ~20-40% toward ~10-15% and tracking 2-6x storm enhancements, by assimilating drag observed on thousands of constellation satellites, so LEO orbit predictions and covariances stay realistic through geomagnetic storms. Storm-time forecast skill beyond about a day stays bounded by CME arrival and magnetic-orientation forecasts.

add_edges.why: Robot-fleet limits are applications of the UGC, k-median and scheduling theorems; they are not 'known' until those are theorems.
Math stops limiting programs only once engineering organizations routinely pose and use AI applied math.
An operating lunar reactor implies a U.S. fission reactor has been launched (FSP/LR-1 satisfies both).
1 GW is ~10,000-14,000 t, ~100-140 Starship flights; not reachable by 2031 without 100+ reusable heavy launches a year.
GW-scale orbital compute runs on commercial accelerators; rad-hard parts cannot supply it.
100 kW-class compute clusters must reject ~100 kW; 100 kW-class radiators have to fly first.
Crew visits to a lunar base need a refueled crewed lander; both HLS architectures refuel in orbit.
A 20 t Mars landing needs a refilled Starship-class vehicle; ship-to-ship transfer must be demonstrated first.
A kg/h ISRU unit on Mars needs a Starship-class landing (node's own rationale).
A Starship-scale propellant plant needs heavy Mars landings.
Life management of fully reusable heavy stages presupposes both stages caught and reflown.
Five ship reflights require ship catch and a first reflight.
The toolchain promises floating-point error bounds for GNC code; that is this capability.
Agents producing GNC code with machine-checked proofs is the toolchain's core step.
A formally verified guidance law needs machine-checked closed-loop stability and safety envelopes.
Verified guidance must hold for the floating-point code that flies.
A verified constellation control plane at commercial scale needs agents that prove real flight and ground code.
Formally verified engine-control software at practical cost needs agents that prove real flight code.
Verified autonomy cannot become cheap unless the cost per verified line collapses.
Replacing structural tests with AI-made analysis needs a defined credibility standard for that evidence.
Certifying each printed part from a digital twin is model-based credit; it needs an accepted evidence standard.
Accepting model-based extrapolation for part of a life requirement needs an accepted evidence standard.

notes: A1 dedupe and cross-link on graph-v0 (360 nodes). 13 merges removing 16 duplicate ids: frontier keeps frontier-math problems (NS unforced, Landau damping, approximation ceilings, optical/quantum capacity, PQ-crypto watch, stiff chemistry, global certificates); verif keeps verification-method and proof-flight nodes (onboard optimizer certificates, lander proof-checked descent, assured RPO, crewed proof certification); capability keeps the shared tier-0 infra-tool-qualification (absorbs verif-checker-not-generator at the scenario premise >2031/2030/2029); plasma keeps thermospheric density (absorbs astro-thermosphere-drag-uq). Each kept node carries a merge_note. Hard edges are added only where the dependent cannot occur without the prerequisite (logical implication, physical necessity such as launch mass or refueling, or an accepted evidence standard for model-based credit); everything else is a soft 'accelerates' edge. Four hard edges were turned soft after merges (public access -> Landau damping; physics theory and certified Pc -> density UQ; capacity theorems -> finite-key QKD proofs). Three year calibrations, each with calibration_note: auton-mars-isru-demo (needs the 2031 heavy Mars landing), verif-afss-part450 and verif-new-entrant-advantage (follow regulator credit for AI proofs). Reviewer flags: (1) auton-mars-isru-demo S2 band Low may now deserve Speculative; (2) verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight bands lowered to Low/Medium/High because the merged node requires guidance-solver proofs as well as fault logic; (3) comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs (Medium/High/High) no longer hard-depends on a Low/Medium/Medium node; (4) infra-tool-qualification could move to S2 2029 if a project takes DO-333 credit for AI-written SPARK/Frama-C proofs in 2028 (verif's upside view).
